properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Pecos River At Pandale Crossing affecting Val Verde County.

Devils River At Cauthorn Ranch Near Juno affecting Val Verde
County.

Devils River At Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pecos River Near Langtry affecting Val Verde County.

Rio Grande At Foster Ranch affecting Val Verde County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pecos River near Langtry.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, (2.1 meters), Lowland flooding reaches into
low areas of the flood plain with no significant damage. At 10.0
feet, (3.0 meters), Minor lowland flooding and turbulence in the
channel is dangerous for inexperienced swimmers, tubers and
canoeists below Pandale to Amistad Reservoir. At 13.0 feet, (4.0
meters), Turbulence in the river channel is dangerous to canoeists
and kayakers. Flow inundates the lower banks of the canyon
threatening sleeping campers and their gear. At 15.0 feet, (4.6
meters), Moderate flooding. Turbulence in the river channel is
dangerous to canoeists and kayakers. Flow inundates the lower banks
of the canyon threatening sleeping campers and their gear.


* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 1.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning to a crest of 15.5 feet early tomorrow
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 815 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 15 at 8:07PM CDT until October 17 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
* WIND...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph behind
a cold front.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum Relative Humidity values between 25 to 40
percent.

* FUELS...Critically dry.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures will
create favorable weather for rapid fire growth and spread. Avoid
activities that promote open flames and sparks.

A Fire Weather Watch means that the potential for critical fire
weather conditions exists. These conditions could promote the
rapid spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening.
Check www.weather.gov/jan/fireweather for forecast updates and a
possible upgrade of this watch to a Red Flag Warning.

properties.areaDesc: Wichita, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 6:31PM CDT until October 15 at 9:30PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Wichita County in northern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 631 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wichita Falls, Sheppard AFB and Pleasant Valley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 15 at 5:24PM MDT until October 16 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Wind Warning, northeast winds 30 to 40 mph with
gusts up to 60 mph expected. For the Blowing Dust Advisory,
visibility between one-quarter and one mile in blowing dust
possible.

* WHERE...Far West Texas and Otero Mesa.

* WHEN...For the High Wind Warning, until noon MDT Friday. For the
Blowing Dust Advisory, until 9 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility.
Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines. Widespread
power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult, especially
for high profile vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Persons with respiratory problems should make preparations to stay
indoors until the storm passes. Be ready for a sudden drop in
visibility to near zero. If you encounter blowing dust or blowing
sand on the roadway or see it approaching, pull off the road as far
as possible and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights all the way
off and keep foot off the brake pedal. Remember, 'Pull Aside, Stay
Alive'.

People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Typhoon Watch issued October 16 at 8:50AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHAMPI CONTINUES WEST-NORTHWEST TOWARD THE
MARIANAS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and recommended
actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Typhoon Watch continues for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan in the
Mariana Islands.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for all of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might be
in effect for your area.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 7 AM ChST...the center of Tropical Storm Champi (29W) was located
near latitude 11.6N...longitude 155.8E. This was about 750 miles
east of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 300 degrees, at 12
mph. Storm intensity was 45 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
When making decisions, do not focus on the exact forecast track. It
is too early to provide exact wind and surge forecast values for
specific locations. A general concern should be for the possibility
of at least extensive damage somewhere within Guam and the Northern
Marianas.
properties.instruction:
Stay calm and keep informed. Comply with any evacuation orders that
are issued for your area. If you live in a metal roof or container
home, or you live in a surge zone or any location prone to flooding,
evacuate to a designated shelter or ride out the storm in the sturdy
home of family or friends outside of evacuation zones.

Items to bring to a shelter include a first aid kit, medicines and
prescriptions, baby food and diapers, games and books, toiletries, a
battery powered radio, a cell phone, flashlights with extra batteries,
a blanket or sleeping bag for each person, personal identification,
copies of key papers such as insurance policies, available cash and
credit cards. Remember, pets are not allowed in most public shelters,
so check ahead with your intended shelter.

Regarding your home or business, cover all windows and doors with
shutters or plywood. Move patio furniture and other loose objects
indoors. Brace all exterior doors, including garage doors. Do this as
early as possible.

If you need to make a trip to the hardware store, the grocery store,
or the gas station, do so as early as possible.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 2:42PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A series of fronts will bring multiple rounds of moderate to heavy
rainfall to the area. The first ongoing front is expected to bring a
total of 0.75 to 1.25 inches of rain to the Juneau area by this
evening, with the second round of heavy rain bringing an additional
1.5 to 2.5 inches through tonight. Localized higher amounts are
possible due to terrain effects. Overall the moderate to heavy
rainfall is expected to last into the overnight hours with little
break in between.

Montana Creek and Jordan Creek are expected to see minor flooding
into Friday morning after these rounds of heavy rainfall. Other
creeks and rivers in the Juneau area will still see rises through
the night into Friday morning, however no flooding is anticipated
for other streams at this time.

For more information on the minor flooding expected for Montana
Creek and Jordan Creek, please see the new Flood Advisory product at
weather.gov/juneau and stay tuned to updates as we continue to
monitor the situation.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 2:23PM AKDT until October 17 at 1:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river storm system moving into the panhandle is
expected to bring two rounds of heavy rainfall to the Juneau area.
The first will continue through today, while the second wave will
bring higher rainfall amounts tonight into Friday morning. This
longer duration of heavy rainfall with not much of a break in between
will allow for river and creek rises, with minor flooding of small
streams expected going into Friday morning.

* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Areas around Montana Creek And Jordan Creek.

* WHEN...Until 130 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Some low-water crossings may become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 PM AKDT, satellite estimates indicate heavy rain across
the advisory area. Rapid river rises will cause minor flooding of
small streams, especially near Montana Creek And Jordan Creek.
Between 0.75 and 1 inch of rain has fallen. The expected rainfall
rate is 0.15-0.3 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of
1.5 to 2.5 inches are possible.

- Montana Creek is anticipated to begin to fall below Minor flood
stage by late Friday morning to midday, while Jordan Creek will
stay above Minor flood stage a bit longer into the day, falling
below Minor flood stage by Friday night.

- For Jordan Creek near Juneau:
At 12:00pm the stage was 7.8 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.7 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.9 feet is expected around 1:00pm
Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around
8:00am. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around
10:00pm.

Impacts:
At 9.2 feet: This is the stage when Jordan Creek is at bankfull and
water will begin to inundate areas along the edges of the creek near
Race Reality and Jordan Square.
At 9.7 feet: Water will inundate the Jordan Square's front and back
parking lots, around Jordan Creek office condominiums with up to one
foot of water. Some residential driveways will be flooded and cut
off.

- For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 12:00pm the stage was 11.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 14.7 feet is expected around 7:00am
Friday. Water levels will go above Minor flood stage around
5:00am. Water levels will go below Minor flood stage around
9:00am.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.
At 15.5 feet: Up to one half foot of water will flow over the low
water crossing on Montana Creek Road after the community gardens.
Water will approach and begin to inundate yards of residences along
the Northwest side of Mendenhall Loop Road.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

If you live near or along Montana Creek or Jordan Creek stay alert
and be prepared to take action.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 1:16PM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH
ANY NEW FIRE STARTS THROUGH SATURDAY, DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY
STRONG SANTA ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Updates include adding the following areas to the previous Red
Flag Warnings - Ojai, Casitas, and the Santa Lucia Mountains.
Moderate to strong Santa Ana winds will peak around Friday then
slowly weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will persist
and dry out any effects of the recent rains. Red Flag Warnings
are in effect for most of Los Angeles and Ventura Counties
Thursday through Saturday, and for interior Santa Barbara and San
Luis Obispo Counties for Friday.

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a
Red Flag Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in
effect until 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Lake Casitas and Ojai Valley.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...East 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 40 mph, strongest Friday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 15 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 12:03PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall to the area. The first ongoing
front is expected to bring 1 to 2 inches of rain to the Juneau area
the rest of today, with the second round of heavy rain bringing an
additional 1 to 2 inches through tonight. More localized higher
amounts are possible due to terrain effects, but overall the
moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to last into the overnight
hours and Friday morning with not much of a break between the rounds
of precipitation.

The precipitation amounts that have fallen today and the additional

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Glacier Bay; Eastern Chichagof Island; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 12:03PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle.
The first ongoing front is expected to bring 1 to 1.5 inches of rain
to the northern half of the panhandle today. The second round of
heavy rain is expected to bring an additional 0.5 to 1.5 inches
tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end QPF amounts
expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More localized lower or
higher amounts are possible due to terrain effects. A brief lull in
the heavier precipitation amounts is expected during the afternoon
hours today.

Even higher rain amounts are possible for parts of the central
panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops
inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of
confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now,
the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof
Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall
amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and
northern panhandle.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 11:40AM PDT until October 16 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 PM THIS EVENING TO 11 AM PDT
FRIDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTH BAY INTERIOR
MOUNTAINS...

.Moderate offshore winds will develop Thursday evening into Friday
morning over the North Bay Interior Mountains. Conditions will be
very dry with very poor overnight humidity recoveries only reaching
14 to 24 percent. Rapid fire spread is possible given the combination
of gusty northerly winds and very dry overnight conditions.

The National Weather Service in San Francisco CA has issued a Red
Flag Warning in effect from 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* AFFECTED AREA...North Bay Interior Mountains.

* TIMING...From 10 PM this evening to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.
The highest peaks above 4000ft will see gusts up to 60 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 16 to 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when weather conditions that promote
rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening are forecast.
This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either
occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple
ways to receive information from authorities.

Please advise responding agencies or fire crews in the field of this
fire weather alert.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How
will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you
call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more
information.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 1:24PM CDT until October 16 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR
properties.description:
...DANGEROUS WILDFIRE CONDITIONS EXPECTED FRIDAY...

The National Weather Service in Little Rock has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Friday.

* WINDS...North to northwest winds 15-20 mph with gusts up to 35
mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...30 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Fires that develop could spread rapidly due to the
strong winds and very dry fuels. Outdoor burning is not
recommended.
properties.instruction:

are either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

of showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and tonight. Heavy
rainfall in short periods of time will bring a risk of flooding
and flash flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Ketchikan Gateway Borough; Annette Island
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 15 at 9:16AM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger atmospheric river continues to move over the panhandle
Thursday, lasting through Friday morning. Multiple waves moving up
will bring persistent moderate to heavy rain for much of the southern
half of the panhandle, with the heaviest rain expected late morning
through the evening hours Thursday. Elevated gusty winds are expected
alongside this heavier rainfall, with the strongest winds expected
Thursday night. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will
produce significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding. Gusty winds alongside the long duration heavy rainfall will
bring a possibility of isolated landslides.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Southern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Ketchikan And Metlakatla.

* WHEN...From 1 PM AKDT this afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.
Isolated landslides are possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday
morning for the Ketchikan and Metlakatla area are still expected
to be around 4 to 6 inches, with higher rain totals favoring
southern facing mountain sides. Highest rain rates are currently
expected during the late morning through evening timeframe on
Thursday, where rates could exceed 0.3 inches per hour.

Confidence has increased for the area seeing winds of 25 to 35
mph with gusts to 55 mph on Thursday at sea level, and exceeding
60 mph at elevation, with the highest winds expected Thursday
evening into the night. With the multiple rounds of moderate to
heavy rainfall and the elevated winds Thursday, there is
possibility for isolated landslides along steep mountain slopes.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Watch for winds and low relative humidity is in effect from
Saturday morning through Saturday evening.

Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire
Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 260
Northern Newton.

CDT Saturday. For the Fire Weather Watch, from Saturday
morning through Saturday evening.

quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can

are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 15 at 9:47AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
AQATWC

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a
PM-10 High Pollution Advisory for Douglas on Friday.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory,
visit the ADEQ internet site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/douglas or
call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 15 at 11:20AM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 9 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from Friday morning
through Sunday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 1
PM Friday to 7 AM CDT Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from
1 PM Friday to 7 AM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is likely to occur during
high tide cycles Friday night, Saturday afternoon, and Saturday
night.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 15 at 10:51AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE SATURDAY...

.A strong cold front will quickly move through the area Friday
afternoon. The front will be mostly if not completely dry as it
moves through the area. Quickly after it moves into the Gulf much
drier air will surge in behind it. In addition cooler air will
move in along with strong northerly winds. On Saturday sunny skies
and winds in the first 1500-3000 ft will be out of the same
direction sllowing for efficient mixing. This will help to bring
wind gusts of 15 to as high as 30 miles an hour across most
locations along and north of I-10. This will also lead to even
drier air mixing into the area helping to drop the RH into the
mid to lower 30% range with some locations seeing the relative
humidity just below 30%. This will combine with current D1 and D2
drought conditions across all of southwest Mississippi and much
of southeast LA along and northwest of a line from Thibodaux to
Franklinton. This could provide ample fuel for wildfires. The
combination of breezy to gusty winds, current drought conditions,
ample fuel, and very dry conditions will allow any fire that
develops to spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pointe Coupee, West Feliciana, East Feliciana,
St. Helena, Washington, Iberville, West Baton Rouge, East
Baton Rouge, Assumption, St. James, Wilkinson, Amite, Pike,
Northern Tangipahoa, Walthall, Southeast St. Tammany, Northern
St. Tammany, Southwestern St. Tammany, Central Tangipahoa,
Lower Tangipahoa, Northern Livingston, Southern Livingston,
Western Ascension and Eastern Ascension.

* WINDS...North 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

Marianas, rapid intensification is possible. This would result in
increased west to southwest monsoon flow will increase. This will
allow for showers to increase in coverage any intensity, with locally
heavy rainfall likely.

At this time, 2 to 4 inches of rainfall may develop, with locally
higher amounts possible. If 29W can intensify a little faster than
anticipated, or if it takes a due west track, this could open door
for isolated wind gusts to 30 to 35 knots to develop. Seas currently
look to increase 1 to 3 feet, topping out near 7 feet, but again,
this could be higher if 29W tracks closer to Chuuk or strengthens
faster.

Folks with intra-island travel should delay any travel for a few
days until the developing tropical depression has passed.

properties.areaDesc: Guam, GU; Rota, MP; Saipan, MP; Tinian, MP
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.
